news.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
paras: Intel asked the U.S. government for a special pass after a rule might stop it from using foreign robots. The robots slide on tracks inside chip factories and carry parts for engineers. These machines come from Japanese companies like Murata and Daifuku.

Because of the new ban, Intel asked for a waiver and got it. The U.S. FCC said Intel could keep using those robots for one year. Intel also can change parts of the robots, making them work safely. These robots help Intel make tiny chips that power smartphones, computers, and cars.

news.title: Atlas Robot’s New Hand May Outperform Humanlike Designs
paras: Robots need a hand that can pick, move, and grip objects easily to help them work in real life. Building such a hand is very hard because it must be strong, flexible, and simple to make. Boston Dynamics says their new robot hand should have three fingers and one thumb.

The hand needs 13 degrees of freedom, meaning 13 movable joints. These joints let the robot grasp objects in many ways, just like a human hand. Because of this design, the robot can pick delicate items without crushing them, making it safer for people.

news.title: 'More missions, more often': NASA is overhauling how it selects science missions
paras: The new approach, called Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), was announced on Oct. 21 in an open letter from Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate (SMD), to the NASA science community.

The changes, directed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, could significantly reshape how scientists, universities, NASA centers and commercial companies vie for future missions. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long," Fox stated in the letter. The new process aims to prioritize scientific merit over unduly complicated engineering and financial planning during initial evaluations, and reduce selection timelines to encourage innovation.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.

They use these colours to represent a competitor at a competition. You wear protective gear in that colour on your stomach. Otherwise, you wear your own white gear. According to sources such as The Korea Herald and Kiddle, Taekwondo is a form of performing art, because you don’t just fight, you learn a pattern.

news.title: Jake Jarman wins two silver medals in British gymnastics first
paras: Jake Jarman has become the first British male gymnast to win two individual medals at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in the Netherlands. The 24-year-old won silver in the men's floor event on Saturday and then another silver in the vault final on Sunday. "The aim is to land on my feet.

sport.title: How much prize money Novak Djokovic could earn for winning the 2026 Basel Open compared to his last appearance
paras: Novak Djokovic is set to make his return to the Basel Open for the first time in 15 years. Djokovic has received a wildcard for the ATP 500 event and will seek to win his 103rd ATP Tour title later this month.

The Serbian star still has a lot to play for this year; after all, he is fighting against the likes of Rafael Jodar and Alex de Minaur for an ATP Finals place. If Djokovic were to win the 2026 Basel Open, the Serb would certainly improve his chances of qualifying while also significantly increasing his prize money total for 2026.

sport.title: ‘Staying healthy is a real skill’: Mouratoglou explains why Zverev deserves to be No. 1
paras: Patrick Mouratoglou believes Alexander Zverev fully deserves his No. 1 ranking, even if Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are better players.

Staying healthy, he argues, is “a real skill” that demands sacrifice, and Zverev’s two Grand Slam titles in 2026 marked a mental breakthrough. Alexander Zverev may not be the best player in the world, but his ranking is fully deserved. That is Patrick Mouratoglou’s view, set out in a video on his social media channels in which he argued that staying healthy is a skill in itself, and part of a player’s value.

paras: Several players won’t be able to finish their seasons strong, though, as they have withdrawn from these two stacked draws. As part of his withdrawal from the entire post- Wimbledon season, Jannik Sinner won’t be participating in Vienna this year.

sport.title: Maja Chwalinska posts message after withdrawing from the Pan Pacific Open, ‘I am very disappointed’
paras: Upon entering the Pan Pacific Open last week, Maja Chwalinska instantly became one of the tournament favourites. The Polish player, who recently won her first WTA Tour title in Wuhan, entered the WTA 500 event as the second seed shortly after withdrawing from the Ningbo Open .

Unfortunately for Chwalinska and her fans, she has been forced to withdraw from the Tokyo-based event due to injury. Chwalinska explained the reason behind her absence in a social media post on Monday. “I am very disappointed to have to withdraw from the Tokyo tournament due to a left thigh injury sustained in Wuhan,” Chwalinska, who was the second seed in Japan, said in an Instagram post on Monday morning.

sport.title: Alex Eala makes interesting prediction about Mika Stojsavljevic after beating her in Tokyo
paras: Alex Eala wasted little time in booking her place in the Pan Pacific Open second round. The Filipina star comfortably defeated British youngster Mika Stojsavljevic on Monday, triumphing 6-1, 6-2 in Tokyo. The result ensures that Eala’s strong record against British players remains intact ; the 21-year-old now has a 5-1 record against players from the island nation.

Following Monday’s contest, Eala offered her instant reaction to the result. “I think it was super important today to be focused in every single point. Playing against Mika for the first time was a great experience, and I’m sure we will meet many, many more times,” Eala said in her on-court interview.

paras: Alex de Minaur will return to action after a rather lengthy rest period, having enjoyed nearly 12 days off following his last match in Shanghai. This should come as no real surprise, given the injury scare he suffered in Beijing.

Having enjoyed an outstanding run in the Chinese capital, he faced Novak Djokovic in the final.
